'''Jinchōkan Moriya Shiryōkan''' (神長官守矢史料館) is a {{ill|Museum|en|Museum|qid=Q33506|lt=museum|1=Museum}} located in {{ill|Miyakawa (Chino City)|ja|宮川 (茅野市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyakawa (Chino City)|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 宮川村 (長野県)|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 宮川村 (長野県)|1=Miyagawa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q17176944}}, {{ill|Chino, Nagano|en|Chino, Nagano|qid=Q838660|lt=Chino City|1=Chino, Nagano}}, {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|en|Nagano Prefecture|qid=Q127877|lt=Nagano Prefecture|1=Nagano Prefecture}}, Japan. The museum preserves and displays documents related to the Moriya family, which served as {{ill|Kancho|ja|神長官|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kancho|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Shinto ritual officials) for the {{ill|Suwa-taisha|en|Suwa-taisha|qid=Q218813|lt=Suwa-taisha|1=Suwa-taisha}} Upper Shrine until the early {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era|1=Meiji era}}. It is situated within the grounds of the Moriya family residence.

== History ==

* In {{ill|1989|en|1989|qid=Q2425|lt=1989|1=1989}}, the 78th head of the Moriya family, {{ill|Moriya Sanae|ja|守矢早苗|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moriya Sanae|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and Chino City requested the design of the museum from architect {{ill|Terunobu Fujimori|en|Terunobu Fujimori|qid=Q3134309|lt=Terunobu Fujimori|1=Terunobu Fujimori}}. Construction was completed in {{ill|1991|en|1991|qid=Q2062|lt=Heisei 3|1=1991}}.<ref>Fujimori's design for the building was initially titled 'Museum of Moriya.'</ref>
* The first director was {{ill|Kosuke Hosoda|ja|細田貴助|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kosuke Hosoda|1=Kisuke Hosoda|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q63958829}}, a local historian and former principal of {{ill|Ochiai Elementary School|ja|富士見町立富士見小学校|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ochiai Elementary School|1=Fujimi Elementary School|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11456192}} in {{ill|Fujimi, Nagano|en|Fujimi, Nagano|qid=Q1204145|lt=Fujimi Town|1=Fujimi, Nagano}}. He served until 1995.
* The current director is Tamura Ken.

== Collection ==

The museum holds significant historical documents, including:
* {{ill|Suwa Daimyōjin Ekotoba|en|Suwa Daimyōjin Ekotoba|qid=Q11631818|lt=Suwa Daimyōjin Ekotoba|1=Suwa Daimyōjin Ekotoba}}
* {{ill|Nenai Shinji Shidai Kyūki|ja|年内神事次第旧記|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nenai Shinji Shidai Kyūki|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* {{ill|Gofureisho|ja|御符礼書|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gofureisho|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
Additionally, it houses letters related to famous samurai such as [[Takeda Shingen]]{{efn|Japanese feudal lord (1521–1573)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeda Shingen|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Takeda Nobumasa|ja|武田信昌|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeda Nobumasa|1=Takeda Nobumasa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q6640068}}, {{ill|Takeda Nobunawa|ja|武田信縄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeda Nobunawa|1=Takeda Nobutsuna|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q6639945}}, {{ill|Murakami Yoshikiyo|en|Murakami Yoshikiyo|qid=Q1048622|lt=Murakami Yoshikiyo|1=Murakami Yoshikiyo}}, and {{ill|Sanada Masayuki|en|Sanada Masayuki|qid=Q1144171|lt=Sanada Masayuki|1=Sanada Masayuki}}.

== Lobby Exhibition Room ==

The lobby features a recreation of offerings for the {{ill|Onbashira Festival|ja|御頭祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onbashira Festival|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, including a deer head.

== Permanent Exhibition Room ==

The permanent exhibition showcases letters and excavated artifacts. These displays are part of rotating exhibits that change every few months. For information on current exhibits, refer to the links below.

== Architecture ==

The building, designed by architect {{ill|Terunobu Fujimori|en|Terunobu Fujimori|qid=Q3134309|lt=Terunobu Fujimori|1=Terunobu Fujimori}}, is a fireproof reinforced concrete structure. It incorporates natural and local materials, including:
* {{ill|Teppeiseki|ja|鉄平石|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Teppeiseki|1=Q11649551|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11649551}} roofing, a traditional technique revived after 50 years
* Siding made of split cypress boards using traditional methods
* Interior elements such as straw-infused mortar and hand-blown glass
Despite its revival of lost traditions, the structure avoids simple historicism, creating a unique and rooted design.<ref name="owari">"End of Architecture / Beginning of Architecture" (INAX Publishing, 2001)</ref>

Nearby, visitors can view other works by Fujimori, including {{ill|Takasugi-an|ja|高過庵|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takasugi-an|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Hikusugi-an|ja|低過庵|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hikusugi-an|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and {{ill|Flying Mud Boat|ja|空飛ぶ泥舟|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Flying Mud Boat|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, though they are generally not open to the public.

== Grounds ==
* '''Gosakuchi Shrine''': A central site of {{ill|Mishaguji|en|Mishaguji|qid=Q11071209|lt=Mishaguji|1=Mishaguji}} worship. Its forest is a designated natural monument of Chino City.
* '''Kaidōden (Prayer Hall)''': Historically used for oral transmission of family secrets, including rituals and genealogies.
* '''Jinchōkan Kofun''': A 7th-century tumulus with a diameter of approximately 9.5m. Artifacts include wooden coffin fragments, swords, and pottery.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.82bunka.or.jp/bunkazai/detail.php?no=1510&seq=0|title=Jinchōkan Kofun|website=82 Cultural Properties Foundation}}</ref>
* '''Ōhōri Suwa Family Cemetery''': A burial site for the Suwa family that later became a communal graveyard.

== Access ==
* About 40 minutes on foot (2.7 km) from {{ill|Chino Station|en|Chino Station|qid=Q844063|lt=Chino Station|1=Chino Station}} ({{ill|East Japan Railway Company|en|East Japan Railway Company|qid=Q499071|lt=JR East|1=East Japan Railway Company}}, Chūō Main Line)
* About 12 minutes on foot (900 m) from "Kami-sha" bus stop on {{ill|Suwa Bus Aruga-Kamisha Route|ja|諏訪バス 有賀・上社統合路線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suwa Bus Aruga-Kamisha Route|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* About 30 minutes on foot (2.2 km) from "Suwa Interchange" bus stop on {{ill|Chūō Expressway Bus Suwa-Okaya Line|ja|中央高速バス 諏訪・岡谷線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chūō Expressway Bus Suwa-Okaya Line|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
